images.caption: A 175g individual of the Millbillillie meteorite shower, a eucrite achondrite that fell in Australia in 1960. This specimen is approx. 6 centimeters wide. Note the shiny black fusion crust with flow lines. The chip at lower right allows one to see the light-gray interior. The orange staining at top is a result of weathering, as these stones were not recovered until many years after they fell.

images.caption: In October of 1960 two station workers witnessed a fireball while opening a gate in the boundary fence on the Millbillillie - Jundee track in Western Australia.  The first pieces of this fall were not recovered until 1970.  Millbillillie is a eucrite and it is recognized by its distinctive orange staining caused by the clay soil.  This complete individual weighs 21.78 grams and has some visible flow features.
